metrics.label: Baltic Supramax Index

metrics.label: Diesel crack vs Brent

brief.text:
The dominant story in today's data is the continuing violence around the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow Gulf waterway through which much Middle East crude and product leaves. gCaptain reports "TARA GAS Burning Off Oman as Another Tanker Attack Leaves 11 Injured", with the LPG tanker still on fire and adrift, while Maritime Executive reports that the US naval blockade now covers vessels that load Iranian cargo at sea. For anyone fixing ships, this is a war-risk and counterparty question before it is a rate question: owners' willingness to send tonnage into Arabian Gulf load ports, and the insurance cost of doing so, is what sets the market.

On today's figures, crude barely moved: Brent at $92.14 a barrel, up 0.19 (+0.2%), and WTI at $83.27, up 0.01, leaving the Brent–WTI spread at $8.87. Bunkers — the fuel ships buy — fell harder, with VLSFO (very low sulphur fuel oil, the standard compliant grade) at $831/t in Singapore, down $31.50 (-3.7%), $705/t in Rotterdam, down $29.00 (-4.0%), $822.50/t in Fujairah, down $9.00 (-1.1%), and $745/t in Houston, down $3.50. The data here does not show why bunkers dropped while crude was flat. Gasoil was $3.95/gal, down 0.6%, with the diesel crack — the refining margin over Brent — at $73.65/bbl. On freight, Hellenic reports clean tanker rates slumping on 18 November, MR (Medium Range product tanker) rates off w125 from the Middle East as Hormuz transits slow; no tanker TCE in our set has refreshed since 15 November, when the VLCC (very large crude carrier) Gulf–China earning was $1,078,714/day and the Suezmax West Africa–UKC $151,300/day. TCE means time charter equivalent, the daily earning a voyage returns.

Running stories: Hormuz escalated again today. Black Sea drone attacks on merchant ships are unchanged with no new headline; dry bulk indices last printed on 18 November with the Baltic Dry Index at 2,914, up 21, and the Capesize index — for the largest iron ore and coal carriers — at 4,549, down 9. Shadow-fleet sanctions and the China port-fee suspension had no news today. New today: Seatrade reports the LA–Long Beach complex bracing for a strike, and MarineLink reports Ukrainian drone strikes cutting Russian refining by 45% since late October.

Watch two things: whether tanker TCEs refresh and how far they have moved since 15 November given the Hormuz disruption, and whether the LA–Long Beach talks fail, since that gateway affects liner and box flows.

storylines.title: Attacks and escalation around Hormuz
storylines.what: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz continue. The LPG tanker TARA GAS remained on fire and adrift off Oman after an attack that left 11 injured, and US guidance has widened a blockade to cover vessels loading Iranian cargo at sea.
storylines.why_it_matters: Hull strikes and blockade guidance raise war-risk premiums for Arabian Gulf liftings, slow transits and shrink the pool of willing owners, reshaping crude, product and gas ton-miles.
storylines.latest: TARA GAS still burning and adrift with 11 injured; US blockade extended to vessels loading Iranian cargo at sea; clean tanker freight reported slumping as Gulf transits slow.

storylines.title: Attacks on shipping in the Black Sea
storylines.what: Drone strikes on merchant ships in the Black Sea have continued through November, with two vessels sunk off Bulgaria and crew injured following an earlier wheat carrier capsizing.
storylines.why_it_matters: Strikes on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling in the region.
sources: Attacks on shipping in the Black Sea

storylines.title: Russian refining damage and diesel export limits
storylines.what: Ukrainian drone attacks have cut Russian refineries' combined crude processing by 45% since late October, on top of a Russian ban on most diesel exports extended to end-January and contested reports of a US-Russia diesel arrangement.
storylines.why_it_matters: Lost Russian refining and export restrictions reshape clean product ton-miles, pulling diesel from longer-haul sources and changing MR and LR employment and crude export balances.
storylines.latest: MarineLink reports Russian crude processing down 45% since late October due to drone strikes.
sources: Ukrainian Drone Attacks Halve Russian Oil Refining in November

storylines.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
storylines.what: Sanctions pressure on the shadow fleet is widening, with EU measures targeting shipowners, managers, insurers and financial networks, adding to earlier US designations.
storylines.why_it_matters: Designations force charterers and underwriters to re-verify counterparties, documents and vessel positions, and can strand tonnage outside compliant trade.
sources: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet

storylines.title: US port fees on Chinese-built and Chinese-operated ships
storylines.what: The US has extended its suspension of port fees targeting Chinese-built and Chinese-operated vessels for another two months while trade talks continue. Separately, a US panel is urging an FMC probe into Chinese port state control detentions of Panama-flagged ships.
storylines.why_it_matters: Reinstated fees or retaliatory detentions would change the cost and risk of deploying particular tonnage into US and Chinese trades and affect chartering preferences across sectors.
storylines.latest: US panel urges an FMC investigation, sanctions and IMO referrals over China's detentions of Panama-flagged ships.

sources: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet

storylines.title: US port fees on Chinese-built and Chinese-operated ships
storylines.what: The US has extended its suspension of port fees targeting Chinese-built and Chinese-operated vessels for another two months while trade talks continue. Separately, a US panel is urging an FMC probe into Chinese port state control detentions of Panama-flagged ships.
storylines.why_it_matters: Reinstated fees or retaliatory detentions would change the cost and risk of deploying particular tonnage into US and Chinese trades and affect chartering preferences across sectors.
storylines.latest: US panel urges an FMC investigation, sanctions and IMO referrals over China's detentions of Panama-flagged ships.
sources: US panel urges FMC probe into China’s PSC vessel detentions

storylines.title: Strike threat at LA-Long Beach
storylines.what: The Los Angeles-Long Beach port complex is bracing for a strike, with employers warning of severe supply chain disruption if last-ditch talks fail.
storylines.why_it_matters: A stoppage at the largest US West Coast gateway would disrupt container flows, berth availability and inland logistics, with knock-on congestion for vessels scheduled to call.
storylines.latest: Seatrade reports employers warning of severe disruption if last-ditch talks fail.
sources: LA-Long Beach port complex braces for strike
